answer: Because the age is read from the hollow checkpoint rather than self-declared, the orchard audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. An identity must be at least 5 epochs old on the ocean ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. Running a farm therefore means funding each extra identity through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent burns once and never again. That is 21 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
